memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and certain Reubenites — Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth — became insolent and rose up against Moses. With them were 250 Israelite men, well-known community leaders who had been appointed members of the council. They came as a group to oppose Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the Lord is with them. Why then do you set yourselves above the Lord's assembly?" — Num 16:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A rebellion is brewing, and it is led not by outsiders but by insiders — Korah, a Levite who already served in God's tabernacle, and 250 respected leaders. These were not nobodies. They held real positions and real honour. Yet discontent had crept into their hearts, and they wanted more.

Notice how they dress up their rebellion in spiritual language. "The whole community is holy... the Lord is with them." Their words sound almost godly. But underneath the pious wrapping was raw envy — a grasping for the authority God had not given them. Some of the most dangerous rebellions come cloaked in religious-sounding words. Not all that speaks of holiness flows from a holy heart.

At its root, this was discontent with God's arrangement. God had assigned Korah a genuine and privileged role among the Levites, but he wanted Aaron's priesthood too. Discontentment is rarely satisfied; give it an inch and it reaches for a mile. It looks past every blessing already received and fixes greedy eyes on what belongs to someone else.

This searches our own hearts. Are we content with the place and calling God has given us, or do we quietly envy the role, gifts, or standing He has given others? True contentment rests in trusting that God assigns each of us wisely and lovingly. The gospel frees us from grasping, because in Christ we already possess every spiritual blessing. We need not seize what is not ours when we know how rich we already are in Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever dressed up envy or ambition in spiritual-sounding language?
2. Are you content with the place and calling God has given you?
3. How does knowing your riches in Christ free you from grasping for more?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart from discontent that dresses itself in holy words. Help me to be content with the place You have given me and to trust that You assign wisely. Thank You that in Christ I already have every blessing I need. Amen.
